title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 138/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 84 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 18 bpm
O2 Saturation: 96% on room air

Recent Labs:
Glucose: 642 mg/dL (Admission)
BUN: 24 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Sodium: 152 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L
Hemoglobin A1c: 9.4%

Review of Systems:
The patient reports significant thirst and frequent urination leading up to admission. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or acute abdominal pain. He denies any recent changes in vision or motor weakness.

Social History:
The patient lives at home with his wife. He retired ten years ago and enjoys gardening. He does not smoke and drinks caffeine occasionally.

Family History:
Father had hypertension and coronary artery disease. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 86-year-old male admitted for a hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state associated with his known type 2 diabetes. Upon admission, he was severely dehydrated with significant laboratory evidence of hyperosmolar status. He was started on aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation and a continuous insulin infusion. Over the course of four days, his glucose levels stabilized and his serum sodium levels normalized. He remained alert and oriented throughout his stay. He tolerated a transition to a subcutaneous insulin regimen and oral hydration. He was cleared for discharge once his metabolic status was stable.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state
2. Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
1. Metformin 500mg BID
2. Lisinopril 10mg daily
3. Insulin Glargine and Lispro as directed

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a blood pressure check and a review of his glucose monitoring logs.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with hyperosmolarity without coma: E11.00 (HCC 36).

distractors.why: A hyperosmolar state is a severe acute complication (HCC 36).
